subject: Insurance
title: The Piper Alpha Oil Rig Explosion
description: A fast breakdown of The Piper Alpha Oil Rig Explosion for builders.

hook.text: In 1988, the Piper Alpha oil platform exploded in the North Sea, killing 167 of 226 workers.

buildup.text: A gas leak ignited during a maintenance miscommunication. The entire platform was engulfed in flames within minutes.

discovery.text: The claim was the largest man-made insured loss at the time. Lloyd's of London syndicates absorbed devastating hits.

twist.text: The disaster led to the Cullen Inquiry, which overhauled offshore safety regulation worldwide.

climax.text: Piper Alpha showed that offshore energy platforms concentrate enormous risk.

punchline.text: 167 dead, $3.4 billion insured. Piper Alpha rewrote offshore safety rules.

quiz.question: What regulatory change followed Piper Alpha?
options: Comprehensive overhaul of offshore safety regulations
